canonical_statement: The primary objective was to determine whether outpatient oral quinolone dispensations were associated with an increased frequency of haemolysis-related diagnosis codes within 30 days compared with oral penicillins.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary objective was to assess whether quinolone dispensations were associated with an increased frequency of haemolysis-related diagnosis codes within 30 days.

canonical_statement: Secondary objectives were to evaluate laboratory changes, paediatric patients, patients exposed to both antibiotic classes, and individual quinolone agents.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary objectives were to examine laboratory changes, paediatric patients, patients exposed to both antibiotic classes and individual quinolone agents.

canonical_statement: The investigators conducted a nationwide retrospective active-comparator cohort study using Clalit Health Services electronic health record data from 1 January 2010 through 31 December 2023.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conducted a retrospective active-comparator cohort study covering 1 January 2010 through 31 December 2023.

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were patients of any age with at least one recorded diagnosis code for G6PD deficiency (D55.0 or D75.A) who received an eligible antibiotic dispensation; laboratory confirmation, enzyme activity, genotype, and variant severity were not required.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A single qualifying code was sufficient; laboratory confirmation, quantitative enzyme activity, genotype and variant severity were not required and were not consistently available.

canonical_statement: The quinolone exposure was an outpatient community dispensation of an oral quinolone (ATC J01M); intravenous administrations were excluded and dispensation was used as a proxy for treatment initiation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exposures were oral quinolones (ATC J01M) and oral penicillins (ATC J01C) dispensed in the community. Intravenous administrations were not included.

canonical_statement: The active comparator was an outpatient community dispensation of an oral penicillin (ATC J01C).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exposures were oral quinolones (ATC J01M) and oral penicillins (ATC J01C) dispensed in the community.

canonical_statement: Dispensation episodes had to be separated by at least 30 days, and episodes in which both antibiotic classes were dispensed within the same 30-day risk window were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Episodes were required to be separated by at least 30 days, and episodes in which both classes were dispensed within the same 30-day risk window were excluded.

canonical_statement: The primary outcome was any haemolysis-related diagnosis code (D59.0, D59.9, D59.10, or D59.13) recorded within 30 days after antibiotic dispensation.

canonical_statement: Supportive laboratory outcomes included haemoglobin change and 30-day thresholds of bilirubin greater than 1.2 mg/dL, LDH greater than 300 U/L, haptoglobin less than 25 mg/dL, and reticulocytes greater than 2.5%.

canonical_statement: Primary regression models adjusted for age at dispensation, sex, and Charlson comorbidity index; binary outcomes used multivariable logistic regression and continuous haemoglobin change used linear regression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary models were adjusted for age at dispensation, sex and Charlson comorbidity index (CCI).

canonical_statement: Laboratory analyses were complete-case analyses; secondary outcomes were exploratory and no multiplicity correction was applied.

canonical_statement: The within-patient sensitivity analysis included patients receiving both antibiotic classes at least 30 days apart and used repeated-measures methods, including generalized estimating equations for episode-level binary outcomes and a patient-level mixed-effects model.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A within-patient sensitivity analysis included patients who received both antibiotic classes at least 30 days apart.

canonical_statement: The paediatric subgroup included patients aged 18 years or younger and used mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, and Charlson comorbidity index.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A paediatric subgroup analysis included patients aged 18 years or younger. Mixed-effects models accounted for repeated episodes and adjusted for age, sex and CCI.

canonical_statement: G6PD deficiency was identified from a single diagnosis code without quantitative enzyme activity or genotype data, creating potential misclassification and limiting applicability to patients with severe deficiency.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The lack of quantitative enzyme activity and genotype data is an important limitation. Requiring only one diagnosis code may include misclassified patients.

canonical_statement: Class-level findings have limited generalizability to rarely used quinolones because nearly all quinolone episodes were ciprofloxacin or ofloxacin, with too few levofloxacin or moxifloxacin episodes for meaningful estimates and no nalidixic acid exposure.
